bug_semantics: Authenticated GET /account/get_following returned each followed user's email in the JSON list. Email is not needed to render the following UI, and sibling followers/search lists already omitted it, so any logged-in user could harvest addresses by following accounts. The patch deletes the email field from that payload.
flaw_origin: 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94 (ecrou-exact, add: [social] notifications, follows, reports, system logs and admin panels) first added get_following() in website/web/account/account.py with items including "email": user.email. Parent 45874f5d162c4dc640f1763cb9916bccaf62b261 already had that file but no get_following route and no that email field. The same BIC commit's get_followers/search_users responses omit email. The field is unchanged until fix 4bad9f105a824979e0ae79fd6115cd7a88c84ee5.

At the fix parent, get_followers and search_users already omit email while get_following includes it. ppa re-checked line-level 2026-08-29: numactl git show 4fa058f^:website/web/account/account.py | grep -c 'get_following' = 0 while BIC 4fa058f adds '/get_following' GET route at line 269 serializing '"email": user.email' at line 282 — vulnerable email leak lines new at BIC. -> introducer_parent_absent=true.
reasoning: The vulnerability is CWE-200 over-disclosure of followed users' emails from get_following. That email field and the endpoint first appear in 4fa058f3, which carries a canonical Claude Sonnet 4.6 co-author trailer. The parent already had account.py without this route. Sibling lists in the same commit omit email, so the leak is novel code on this surface, not a later copy. AI wrote the defective field, so the verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE. The later human fix only removes that field and does not change BIC authorship.
